passage: In the Monday review at the Gurugram office, Chandrika clicked to slide seven and said, "Our idea is a referral bonus for repeat clients." Sachin's coffee stopped halfway to his mouth. He had emailed that exact plan three weeks ago, with a costing sheet. His ears burned, and he wanted to say "that's mine" right there. He did not. Afterwards, in the pantry, he said quietly, "Chandrika, that idea was in my mail on the ninth. I would have liked a mention." She flushed and said she had "built on it." That evening Sachin printed the email trail and began sending weekly updates to the whole team in writing. He did not go to the manager yet. If it happened again, he would.

qa.q: When had Sachin emailed the referral bonus plan?
qa.a: Sachin emailed it on the ninth, three weeks earlier.

qa.q: What was Sachin feeling when Chandrika presented slide seven?
qa.a: Anger and a sense of being cheated: his ears burned and he wanted to say "that's mine."

qa.q: What could Sachin do if it happens again?
qa.a: Take the printed email trail and the written updates to the manager.

qa.q: How might Chandrika have felt when Sachin spoke to her in the pantry?
qa.a: She flushed and said she had "built on it," which suggests embarrassment or defensiveness.

grounding: A colleague presents the protagonist's idea as their own; he speaks privately, keeps records, moves to written updates and will escalate if repeated.
